subject: words
title: Un- and re-
about: Words built from a base word he can read plus a prefix that carries a meaning: un- means not (unhappy) and re- means again (redo). NC L.1.4 asks him to use word parts to work out new words and names re- as its example; CKLA Grade 1 has no prefix lessons, so open this level once he reads two-part words comfortably (after Unit 4).
tip: Cover the prefix with a finger, read the base word, then uncover it and ask: so what does the whole word mean?

cards.note: un- means not: unhappy is not happy. The y at the end says long e.
un- means not or undo it: unlock is to open the lock.
un- means undo it: untie is to undo the knot. In tie the ie says long i.
un- means undo it: unzip is to open the zip.
un- means undo it: unpack is to take things out of the bag.
un- means take it back: undo is to make it like before. do is a tricky word: the o says oo.
un- means not: unkind is not kind. In kind the i says its name.
un- means not: unfair is not fair. air says air.
un- means not: unsafe is not safe. Magic e makes the a say its name.
un- means undo it: unwrap is to take the paper off. wr says r.
un- means undo it: unplug is to pull the plug out.
re- says ree and means again: redo is to do it again. do is a tricky word: the o says oo.
re- means again: replay is to play it again. ay says long a.
re- means again: retell is to tell the story again.
re- means again: refill is to fill it up again.
re- means again: reread is to read it again. ea says long e here.
re- means again: rewrite is to write it again. wr says r, magic e makes the i say its name.
re- means again: repaint is to paint it again. ai says long a.
re- means again: reuse is to use it again. In use the u says its name.
re- means again: rebuild is to build it again. In build the ui says short i: bild.
